faq.q: How do I convert a PDF to RTF?

guide.intro: RTF is Rich Text Format – the universal word-processor format that opens in Word, WordPad, TextEdit, LibreOffice, Pages and Google Docs. {brand} turns a PDF into a clean, editable RTF document directly in your browser – reading order, headings, bold/italic, lists, tables and images are reconstructed.
uses: Edit a PDF in LibreOffice, WordPad or TextEdit without Microsoft Word.
Submit documents to offices that require ODF or RTF.
Recover the text of scanned letters with OCR.
Re-use content from reports and brochures.
tips: Choose the correct OCR language for scanned pages.
Multi-column pages are converted in reading order; check headings afterwards.
For a perfect visual copy, use PDF to Word (Exact layout).
more: pdf.js extracts every text run with its font, size and position; the same engine as our PDF to Word tool groups runs into lines, paragraphs, columns and tables, detects headings by size and weight, and embeds images. The document is then written as RTF – entirely on your device.
Compared with iLovePDF, Smallpdf, Adobe and Sejda

Most of them don’t offer RTF output at all, or only via upload with daily limits (Sejda: 3 tasks per hour, 50 MB; Smallpdf: a couple per day). OCR is usually a paid feature – here it is free and local.

faq.a: Yes, once the page and the OCR language data have loaded.
Yes – text is stored as Unicode, so any script is preserved.
